exposure: Gestational age: < 27 weeks, 27-29 weeks and > 30 weeks
cohort: 447 preterm infants < 35 weeks gestation admitted to the neonatal intensive care unit
finding: The rate of delayed cord clamping was low, particularly among extremely preterm infants, and infants not receiving delayed cord clamping were smaller, of lower gestational age, and more likely to be delivered via cesarean section.
mod_finding: Infants not receiving delayed cord clamping were more likely to be delivered via cesarean section.
birth_weight: Not specified, but infants not receiving DCC were smaller
